clue.text: See 24
Film director's half of winter sport gear (ends of tie cord separately removed)

indicators.note: the two letters come out of different places in the phrase, one from each of two words, hence separately

parts.note: a skier's gear is poles and skis; one of each, half the full kit, is written POLE AND SKI

indicators.note: the ends of tie and cord are their final letters, which are the ones taken away

explanation.surface: A film director's ski kit is missing bits, with the tie cord's ends cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' is a link: one pole and one ski are half the kit. 'ends of' gives E and D, which 'separately removed' takes from POLE and AND, leaving POL + AN + SKI.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman Polanski is the Polish-French film director of Chinatown and The Pianist; the clue's possessive is a link.

clue.text: House dog's guts worn

indicators.note: the guts of a phrase are its insides, so the answer is found running inside the words house dog

explanation.surface: A house dog's insides are described as worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something used is second-hand or worn from previous handling, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Sophisticated, emergent girl broadcasting

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young woman making her entrance, or emerging, into high society
a programme being broadcast is on air

explanation.surface: A sophisticated young woman appears on the radio for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: A debutante is a girl formally introduced into upper-class society, traditionally at a London ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair describes a man of suave, confident sophistication and charm, a direct synonym.

clue.text: See 28
Not quite captains' stools

definitions.meaning: second-in-command figures rank just below the captains of a team or ship
stools in the medical sense are faeces, which children's slang calls by this name

explanation.walkthrough: The plural possessive 'captains'' is part of the first definition's surface; 'number two' is a deputy and also nursery slang for a bowel movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Deputies sit second in rank behind captains, and nursery euphemism uses the same phrase for faeces, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Without a greeting, one gets food

indicators.note: without signals that the letter a is dropped from the greeting word

parts.note: a salaam is a Muslim greeting of peace, often with a low bow
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone who skips saying hello still gets something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a cured, spiced sausage, an example of food.

clue.text: See 18
See 12
Being rather archaic, cry out audibly: "Hey, Mr Frost, you dead!"

indicators.note: audibly tells us the phrase is spoken, and its sound is what goes in the grid

parts.note: hey is EH; Jack Frost personifies frost, so Mr Frost is JACK; you is YOU; dead is LATE, as in the late king

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims old-fashionedly over the death of Jack Frost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being rather archaic' warns that 'cry out' is a dated sense of the answer; 'audibly' says EH JACK YOU LATE is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic meaning of the verb is to exclaim or blurt suddenly, which is to cry out.

clue.text: About to tie up Spike outside a detainee's place

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the whole string round, reading the pieces backwards together

parts.note: to moor a boat is to tie it up

indicators.note: outside means the drug word wraps around the letter a

parts.note: to spike a drink is to drug it

explanation.surface: An instruction to restrain a spiky character outside a prisoner's cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' reverses the whole run at once, so the second half of the clue becomes the first half of the answer; 'Spike' is the verb to tamper with a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardroom is where soldiers under arrest are held, so it is a place for a detainee.

clue.text: One wouldn't be pleased to give them Jet Air South

definitions.text: One wouldn't be pleased to give them

parts.note: jet is an intensely black stone, so jet black is a deep black
an air is a look or manner, as in an air of confidence
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Someone is displeased by an airline called Jet Air South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jet Air' reads as an airline's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Black looks are glowering, disapproving glances, given by someone who is displeased.

clue.text: Jonathan's going to each extension of the Pacific Ocean

parts.note: Jonathan Ross is a British TV and radio presenter; his name with the possessive gives the surname plus S
ea is a standard abbreviation for each, as on price tags

explanation.surface: A TV presenter is heading off to each corner of the Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan Ross is a well-known British chat-show host; here the possessive 's is kept as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ross Sea is a deep bay of the Southern Ocean off Antarctica, south of the Pacific, so the clue calls it an extension of it.

clue.text: See 26
Carrots often included in concentrated drinks

definitions.meaning: carrots dangled before someone are inducements or bribes
fruit squashes and cordials usually contain added sugar or artificial sugar substitutes

explanation.walkthrough: Carrot-and-stick gives 'carrots' as incentives; the second definition describes the additives in squash, a British concentrated fruit drink diluted with water.
explanation.definitionFit: Inducements that make a deal more attractive and substances that make drinks taste sugary share this name.

clue.text: Career over, squeal: "It's a profession!"

indicators.note: over says the running word is turned back to front

parts.note: to career is to run headlong
to squeal on someone is to inform, which slang also calls singing

explanation.surface: An informer whose career is finished declares that grassing counts as a profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' looks like a noun meaning a job; here it is the verb to rush.
explanation.definitionFit: Caring for the sick as a trained professional is a recognised profession.

clue.text: Olive, possibly, seen with comedian's insurance document

parts.note: olive is one shade of green, hence possibly
a card is a joker or comic person

explanation.surface: Olive appears in a comedian's insurance papers.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a green card was the certificate proving motor insurance valid abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The international motor insurance certificate carried when driving abroad was known by this name.

clue.text: See 20
US reactionary's date with (finally) Jonathan Creek broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters are thrown into a new order
finally picks only the last letter of the name Jonathan

explanation.surface: A US conservative has a date while the TV show Jonathan Creek is on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' scrambles D, N (from 'finally' Jonathan) and CREEK. Jonathan Creek is a British TV mystery series.
explanation.definitionFit: A redneck is a derogatory US term for a poor, rural, politically reactionary white person.

clue.text: Begrudge getting out software fixer

indicators.note: getting out suggests the letters breaking loose and falling into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone resents leaving the IT technician.
explanation.definitionFit: A debugger is a program that helps find and remove errors from code.

clue.text: Barry (associated with hooter) muffling one background sound?

parts.note: Barry White was an American soul singer with a famously deep voice

indicators.note: muffling means wrapping round, so the nose word encloses the letter for one

parts.note: hooter is slang for the nose
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A singer linked to a big nose is muffling someone in the background.
explanation.definitionFit: White noise is a steady hiss of all frequencies often played as background sound to mask other noises.

clue.text: Bold — just the thing to mask masculine ways

indicators.note: to mask means to cover over, so the thing word wraps round the others

parts.note: it means just the thing, as in that's it
M is the grammatical abbreviation for masculine
modes are ways or methods

explanation.surface: A bold remark says something suits for hiding male habits.
explanation.definitionFit: Immodest behaviour is forward or brazen, matching bold in its sense of shameless.

clue.text: Just once, do put one out!

parts.note: ex means former, so once, as in an ex-husband
to do is to act

indicators.note: out means the letter for one is removed from the putting word

parts.note: to lay something is to put it down
a means one, as in a dog

explanation.surface: A one-time instruction to extinguish something.
explanation.definitionFit: Just, as in just so, means precisely, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Main ways to give impolite US women a new start

indicators.note: a new start replaces the first letter of the slang word with the letter given before it

parts.note: broads is dated, disrespectful American slang for women
the letter a is the replacement

explanation.surface: Advice on how to give rude American women a fresh beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: A-roads are Britain's main roads, ranking below motorways.
explanation.definitionFit: In the UK road system, A-roads are the main trunk routes, so they are main ways.

clue.text: Wimpish Iris's quarantine indicator?

parts.note: yellow is slang for cowardly or wimpish
a flag is a kind of iris, the yellow flag being a common wild one

explanation.surface: Iris the coward is a sign of an infectious disease.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow flag flown by a ship signals quarantine or a request for health clearance, so it is a quarantine signal.

clue.text: Knot-tying supporter's stem set in bar

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the bar word

parts.note: to bar is to ban

indicators.note: set means arranged, so the letters of stem are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A stem is fixed in a bar holding a knot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' scrambles the stem and 'in' places the result inside the bar word; 'Knot-tying' points to a wedding, not a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Tying the knot is getting married, and the groom's chief supporter at a wedding has this title.

clue.text: Yes-man enters two names and round figure in Internet Explorer?

indicators.note: enters means the two names and figure go inside the program word

parts.note: Internet Explorer is an example of a web browser, hence the question mark
n is the abbreviation for name, so two of them give NN
the round figure is the letter O, shaped like a zero

explanation.surface: A sycophant types two names and zero into a web browser.
explanation.definitionFit: A brown-noser is a sycophant who flatters superiors, like a yes-man who always agrees.

clue.text: Shock colouring of some elderly people being racier in Kent area?

definitions.text: Shock colouring of some elderly people

parts.note: ... means risqué, so ... is racier
Kent is a county in South East England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: Older people are getting naughtier in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' here is a mass of hair. Kent is an English county in the south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue rinse is a tinted hair dye worn by some older women to tone grey hair, a colouring of their shock of hair.

clue.text: Police dog purged of speech therapy

indicators.note: purged suggests a shake-out, so the letters of police dog are rearranged

explanation.surface: A police dog has been cleared of a speech treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Logopedics is a term for speech therapy, and this adjective means relating to it.

clue.text: Pacific food fish, scallops and tree fruit kernel (not date)

parts.note: to ... fabric is to cut a scalloped or zigzag edge, so ... means scallops

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the letter for date

parts.note: an almond is the kernel of the almond tree's fruit

explanation.surface: A menu of Pacific fish, scallops and almonds without dates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scallops' looks like seafood, but it is the verb to cut wavy edges.
explanation.definitionFit: The pink salmon, or humpback, is a Pacific salmon caught widely for food.

clue.text: See 16
Experienced, possibly half-baked, wanting $1,000 for date

indicators.note: for says the grand comes in place of the date letter

parts.note: half-baked food is possibly not cooked enough
a thousand dollars is a grand, abbreviated G

explanation.surface: A half-baked plan, wanting a thousand dollars for a date.
explanation.definitionFit: Something undergone has been experienced or gone through, a direct synonym.

clue.text: See 26
